title: Week 34 Mastery Quiz · Thesis Drafting and Peer Review

questions.question: A thesis draft argues that a legal right is effective solely because the constitution contains it. What evidence should the reviewer request?
options: A longer definition of the right.
The title of the constitution.
Implementation records, access barriers, relevant judgments and outcomes.
The number of pages in the thesis.
questions.explanation: Implementation records, access barriers, relevant judgments and outcomes.

questions.question: A peer reviewer receives a claim without any source date or article reference. What is the most actionable response?
options: Approve the claim if it sounds plausible.
Replace it with a party position.
Delete all supporting evidence.
Request precise provenance and the source passage supporting the claim.
questions.explanation: Request precise provenance and the source passage supporting the claim.

questions.question: A senior cites UDHR Article 10 but concludes it proves every tribunal is impartial. What revision is required?
options: Separate the stated normative principle from observed tribunal performance.
Treat the UDHR as a census of courts.
Remove Article 10 from the bibliography.
Assume impartiality is unmeasurable.
questions.explanation: Separate the stated normative principle from observed tribunal performance.

questions.question: A literature review summarizes authors but does not compare their arguments. What strengthens synthesis?
options: Add more biographical facts.
Identify shared questions, competing mechanisms, evidence standards and research gaps.
Arrange the authors by surname only.
Avoid discussing any disagreement.
questions.explanation: Identify shared questions, competing mechanisms, evidence standards and research gaps.

questions.question: A peer reviewer challenges the sample selection but the draft provides no rationale. Which repair is appropriate?
options: Assert that famous cases require no rationale.
Remove methods from the paper.
Explain why cases were chosen, likely biases and the claim's generalizability limits.
Change the sample size in the title.
questions.explanation: Explain why cases were chosen, likely biases and the claim's generalizability limits.

questions.question: A methods section calls a descriptive trend a controlled experiment. What correction protects validity?
options: Keep the term experiment for prestige.
Label any chart a randomized trial.
Conclude causality from the graph alone.
Accurately identify the observational design and its limitations on causal claims.
questions.explanation: Accurately identify the observational design and its limitations on causal claims.

questions.question: A senior discovers two credible sources disagree over the year a policy took effect. What belongs in the revision memo?
options: The conflicting dates, authoritative chronology checked and justified final wording.
Only the preferred date.
An unmarked replacement of one source.
A claim that disagreement proves both false.
questions.explanation: The conflicting dates, authoritative chronology checked and justified final wording.

questions.question: An essay quotes a public document but the quotation omits a qualification. What should the author do?
options: Retain the shortened wording without notation.
Restore necessary context and distinguish verbatim text from paraphrase.
Present a paraphrase inside quotation marks.
Discard the source's document identifier.
questions.explanation: Restore necessary context and distinguish verbatim text from paraphrase.

questions.question: A statistical appendix uses percentages rounded differently in the text and figures. What is a sound editorial response?
options: Choose the largest displayed percentage.
Remove denominators.
Recalculate from underlying values and use a consistent explained rounding policy.
Change data to fit a chart.
questions.explanation: Recalculate from underlying values and use a consistent explained rounding policy.

questions.question: A final revision adds a counterargument but no answer to it. Which further step best demonstrates senior reasoning?
options: Label the counterargument irrational.
Delete the counterevidence.
Claim that the thesis title settles the dispute.
Represent the counterargument fairly, test supporting evidence and explain the qualified response.
questions.explanation: Represent the counterargument fairly, test supporting evidence and explain the qualified response.

shortResponse: How can revision improve reasoning, evidence, organization, fairness, and academic integrity?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
